issues.detail: The Greek verb 'ερουσιν' (erousin) is in the present tense, indicating a repeated or habitual action ('many will say to me...'), whereas the Vietnamese 'sẽ nói' (will say) is simple future. More importantly, the Vietnamese adds a question mark and 'chẳng từng' (never/didn't ever), turning the Greek statement of fact into a rhetorical question of denial that isn't present in the Greek structure.
